get_address.description: Get what a Bitcoin address holds and what has passed through it: its balance, everything ever received and sent, and how many transactions have touched it. Money still waiting to confirm is reported separately from money that has settled, because only one of them is yours to spend. The step behind a treasury report or a 'has the payment arrived' check. No API key required.
get_address.display_str_template: Get the balance of Bitcoin address {0}.
get_address.name: get_address

parameters.description: The address to look at, exactly as it was given to you. Bitcoin has several address formats and all of them work here: bc1q… and bc1p… (the modern ones), and the older 1… and 3…. Capitalisation matters everywhere except in a bc1 address, so paste rather than retype.
parameters.name: address

address_summary.description: What an address holds, and what has passed through it.

balance_btc.description: What it holds right now, counting pending transactions. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

balance_sats.description: What it holds right now, counting pending transactions. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

confirmed_balance_btc.description: What it holds in settled money, ignoring anything still pending. This is the figure to act on. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

confirmed_balance_sats.description: What it holds in settled money, ignoring anything still pending. This is the figure to act on. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

pending_balance_btc.description: The net effect of its unconfirmed transactions. Negative when it is in the middle of spending. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

pending_balance_sats.description: The net effect of its unconfirmed transactions. Negative when it is in the middle of spending. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

pending_transaction_count.description: How many of its transactions are still waiting to confirm.

total_received_btc.description: Everything ever paid into it, over its whole life. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_received_sats.description: Everything ever paid into it, over its whole life. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

total_sent_btc.description: Everything ever spent out of it. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_sent_sats.description: Everything ever spent out of it. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

transaction_count.description: How many confirmed transactions have touched it.

unspent_output_count.description: How many separate coins make up its balance. 'List unspent outputs' lists them.

get_block.description: Get one block by its height or its hash: when it was mined, which pool found it, how many transactions it settled and what they paid. Paste whichever of the two you have - it works out which. No API key required.
get_block.name: get_block

parameters.description: Either the block's height - its number, such as 800000 - or its 64-character hash. Whichever you have is fine; this works out which one you gave it.
parameters.name: block

block.description: One block: a batch of transactions settled onto the chain.

difficulty.description: How hard it was to mine, at the difficulty in force then.

height.description: Its number, counting from the first block ever mined. This is what people mean by 'block 800,000'.

median_fee_rate_sat_vb.description: The middle fee rate paid by the transactions in it, in sat/vB.

merkle_root.description: The fingerprint of everything in it.

mined_by.description: The mining pool that found it, e.g. 'Foundry USA'. 'Unknown' where the pool cannot be identified, and null for the few blocks mempool.space has not attributed.

previous_block_hash.description: The hash of the block before it, which 'Get a block' also takes.

reward_btc.description: What the miner earned: the block subsidy plus those fees. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

reward_sats.description: What the miner earned: the block subsidy plus those fees. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

timestamp.description: When it was mined. As unix seconds.

timestamp_iso.description: When it was mined. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

total_fees_btc.description: What every transaction in it paid in fees. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_fees_sats.description: What every transaction in it paid in fees. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

get_historical_price.description: Get what one bitcoin was worth at a past moment. Pick the date and time and this finds the closest price mempool.space has, and tells you which moment that price is from. The step to put after 'Get a transaction' to value a payment at the moment it confirmed, for a ledger, an invoice or a tax record. No API key required.
get_historical_price.display_name: Get the bitcoin price on a date
get_historical_price.name: get_historical_price

parameters.description: The moment to price bitcoin at. Mempool.space keeps hourly prices for recent years and daily prices for the earlier ones, and answers with the closest it has - the result says exactly which moment its price is from. Its index starts in 2010.
parameters.name: date_time

parameters.description: Which currency to price bitcoin in. US dollars unless you say otherwise.
parameters.name: currency

price.description: What one bitcoin was worth at that moment.

price_at.description: The moment this price is actually from - the closest one mempool.space has to what you asked for. As unix seconds.

price_at_iso.description: The moment this price is actually from - the closest one mempool.space has to what you asked for. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

requested_at.description: The moment you asked about. As unix seconds.

requested_at_iso.description: The moment you asked about. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

get_network_congestion.description: Check how busy Bitcoin is: how many transactions are waiting to be mined, how much room they need, and how many blocks it would take to clear them. When the backlog is deep, cheap transactions wait - so this is the step to check before sending anything, or to post to a channel when the network gets busy. No API key required.
get_network_congestion.name: get_network_congestion
get_network_congestion.result_str_template: {mempool_space_get_network_congestion,transactions_waiting} transactions waiting, about {mempool_space_get_network_congestion,projected_blocks_to_clear} blocks to clear.

next_block_median_fee_rate_sat_vb.description: The middle fee rate among the transactions expected in the next block, in sat/vB.

items.description: One block mempool.space expects to be mined next, from what is waiting.

median_fee_rate_sat_vb.description: The middle fee rate of those transactions, in sat/vB.

total_fees_btc.description: What those transactions would pay in fees. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_fees_sats.description: What those transactions would pay in fees. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

transaction_count.description: How many waiting transactions would fit in it.

projected_blocks_capped.description: True when the backlog is deeper than mempool.space projects, so the block count above is a floor rather than an estimate.

projected_blocks_to_clear.description: How many blocks mempool.space expects it will take to clear the backlog - roughly ten minutes each.

size_vmb.description: How much room everything waiting would take, in virtual megabytes. A block holds about one, so this is the backlog measured in blocks' worth.

total_fees_waiting_btc.description: What every waiting transaction has offered in fees. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_fees_waiting_sats.description: What every waiting transaction has offered in fees. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

transactions_waiting.description: How many transactions have been broadcast but not yet mined. A few thousand is quiet; tens of thousands is busy.

get_network_status.description: Get the health of the Bitcoin network: how much computing power is securing it, how hard mining currently is, and when the difficulty next changes and by how much. Difficulty adjusts every two weeks and the estimate moves all the way up to the day, so this is the step behind a mining report or a network dashboard. No API key required.
get_network_status.name: get_network_status
get_network_status.result_str_template: Hashrate {mempool_space_get_network_status,hashrate_eh_s} EH/s. Difficulty changes in {mempool_space_get_network_status,blocks_until_adjustment} blocks.

blocks_until_adjustment.description: How many blocks are left before difficulty changes.

days_until_adjustment.description: How many days away that is.

difficulty.description: How hard it currently is to mine a block.

difficulty_change_percent.description: How much difficulty is expected to move at the next adjustment, as a percentage. Positive means mining gets harder. This estimate moves until the moment it happens.

hashrate_eh_s.description: How much computing power is mining Bitcoin, in exahashes per second - the unit mining reports use. This is the readable figure.

hashrate_hs.description: The same figure in raw hashes per second.

next_adjustment_at.description: When that is expected to happen. As unix seconds.

next_adjustment_at_iso.description: When that is expected to happen. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

next_adjustment_height.description: The block height at which it will change.

previous_change_percent.description: How much it moved at the last adjustment.

progress_percent.description: How far through the current two-week period we are.

get_price.description: Get what one bitcoin is worth right now, in your choice of seven currencies - and in all seven at once, so one step can price a report for several regions. The number behind a daily price post, a portfolio total or a threshold alert. No API key required.
get_price.name: get_price

parameters.description: Which currency to price bitcoin in. US dollars unless you say otherwise.
parameters.name: currency

as_of.description: When this price was published. As unix seconds.

as_of_iso.description: When this price was published. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

price.description: What one bitcoin is worth in that currency.

prices.description: The price in every currency mempool.space quotes, keyed by currency code.

get_recommended_fees.description: Get what a Bitcoin transaction needs to pay right now to confirm, at each level of hurry - next block, within half an hour, within an hour, and the two economy rates. All in sat/vB, the unit every wallet asks for. Fees swing by an order of magnitude in a day, so this is the step behind 'send when it's cheap' and 'tell me when fees spike'. No API key required.
get_recommended_fees.name: get_recommended_fees

economy_sat_vb.description: Cheap, and it may take many hours or longer. Fine for anything not in a hurry.

fastest_sat_vb.description: Pay this to be in the very next block - about ten minutes. The rate to use when it has to land now.

half_hour_sat_vb.description: Pay this to confirm within about half an hour.

hour_sat_vb.description: Pay this to confirm within about an hour.

minimum_sat_vb.description: The least the network will currently relay. Below this a transaction may never be passed on at all.

get_transaction.description: Get one Bitcoin transaction: whether it has confirmed and how many times, what it moved and between which addresses, and what it paid in fees. The step behind 'wait for three confirmations before shipping' and 'did that payment actually go through'. No API key required.
get_transaction.name: get_transaction

parameters.description: The transaction's id: 64 characters, made up of the digits 0-9 and the letters a-f. Every wallet and every explorer calls it the same thing, so this is what a receipt, a support ticket or an earlier step will have given you.
parameters.name: txid

transaction.description: One Bitcoin transaction. The same shape wherever it was found - looked up on its own, on an address, or read out of a block.

block_hash.description: The hash of the block it was mined into, or null while pending.

block_height.description: The number of the block it was mined into, or null while pending.

block_time.description: When that block was mined. As unix seconds.

block_time_iso.description: When that block was mined. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

confirmations.description: How many blocks have been mined on top of it, counting its own. 0 while it is still waiting. Six is the usual bar for treating a payment as final; one is enough for most everyday amounts.

confirmed.description: Whether this is in a block yet. False means it is still waiting in the mempool: broadcast and seen by the network, but not settled.

explorer_url.description: Its page on mempool.space, for a person to open.

fee_btc.description: What the sender paid the miner to include it. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

fee_rate_sat_vb.description: What it paid per virtual byte, in sat/vB - the unit every fee estimate is quoted in, so this compares directly against 'Get recommended fees'.

fee_sats.description: What the sender paid the miner to include it. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

input_count.description: How many inputs it has, in total.

inputs.description: Its inputs, up to the first 25. Almost every transaction has a handful.

items.description: One input: a coin this transaction spent, and where it came from.

address.description: The address the money came from. Null for newly minted coin and for the handful of outputs that have no address form.

from_output_index.description: Which output of that transaction this coin was.

from_txid.description: The transaction this coin came out of.

is_new_coin.description: True for the miner's reward, which is newly created bitcoin rather than a spend of anything, and so has no source address.

replaceable.description: Whether this input was marked as replaceable, letting the sender replace the transaction with a higher-fee one.

value_btc.description: What this input was worth. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

value_sats.description: What this input was worth. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

inputs_truncated.description: True when it has more inputs than are listed above. The input count is always the real one.

output_count.description: How many outputs it has, in total.

outputs.description: Its outputs, up to the first 25.

items.description: One output: money this transaction paid out, and to where.

address.description: The address paid. Null when the output is data rather than a payment - see the type below.

output_index.description: Its position in the transaction, counting from 0. This is what 'Check whether outputs have been spent' reports against.

type.description: How the output is locked, in the service's own shorthand: v0_p2wpkh, v1_p2tr, p2pkh, op_return and so on.

type_label.description: The same thing in words: 'Native SegWit (P2WPKH)', 'Taproot (P2TR)', 'Data, not a payment (OP_RETURN)'.

value_btc.description: What was paid to it. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

value_sats.description: What was paid to it. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

outputs_truncated.description: True when it has more outputs than are listed above.

replaceable.description: True while the sender can still replace this transaction with a higher-fee one, which is why a payment is not final until it confirms. Meaningless once confirmed.

size_bytes.description: Its size on disk, in bytes.

total_out_btc.description: The total it paid out, across all outputs. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_out_sats.description: The total it paid out, across all outputs. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

txid.description: Its 64-character transaction id, which is how it is referred to everywhere. 'Get a transaction' takes one of these.

vsize.description: Its virtual size in vB, which the fee rate is quoted against.

weight.description: Its weight units, the measure blocks are filled by.

get_transaction_outspends.description: Check, for each of a transaction's outputs, whether the money has been moved on again - and by which transaction. The step that answers 'has the recipient touched what we sent them' and 'is that coin still where we left it', which a balance alone cannot tell you. No API key required.
get_transaction_outspends.display_name: Check whether outputs have been spent
get_transaction_outspends.display_str_template: Check the outputs of Bitcoin transaction {0}.
get_transaction_outspends.name: get_transaction_outspends

parameters.name: txid

all_spent.description: True when every output has been moved on. The field to branch on for 'has it all been swept'.

output_count.description: How many outputs the transaction has.

outputs.description: Each output, in the order the transaction lists them.

items.description: One of the transaction's outputs, and whether it has moved on.

block_height.description: The number of the block it was mined into, or null while pending.

block_time.description: When that block was mined. As unix seconds.

block_time_iso.description: When that block was mined. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

confirmations.description: How many blocks have been mined on top of it, counting its own. 0 while it is still waiting. Six is the usual bar for treating a payment as final; one is enough for most everyday amounts.

output_index.description: Its position in the transaction, counting from 0.

spent.description: Whether this output has been spent by a later transaction. False means the money is still sitting where this transaction put it.

spent_by_explorer_url.description: The spending transaction's page on mempool.space.

spent_by_txid.description: The transaction that spent it, or null if nothing has.

spent_count.description: How many of them have been spent onward.

txid.description: The transaction whose outputs these are.

unspent_count.description: How many are still sitting where this transaction put them.

list_address_transactions.description: List the most recent transactions at a Bitcoin address, newest first, with what each one moved and how many confirmations it has. Include the ones still waiting to confirm and you see a payment the moment it is broadcast, rather than ten minutes later. The step to run on a schedule to watch an address for incoming money. No API key required.

list_address_utxos.description: List the individual coins sitting at a Bitcoin address, each with its own value and how many confirmations it has, plus what they add up to. Bitcoin holds a balance as separate coins rather than one number, and a wallet has to spend whole ones - so this is what a spend actually has to work with, and what a coin-management or consolidation workflow reads. Addresses holding more than 500 coins are more than mempool.space's public API will list; 'Get an address balance' still counts them. No API key required.
list_address_utxos.display_str_template: List unspent coins at Bitcoin address {0}.
list_address_utxos.name: list_address_utxos

parameters.description: The address to look at, exactly as it was given to you. Bitcoin has several address formats and all of them work here: bc1q… and bc1p… (the modern ones), and the older 1… and 3…. Capitalisation matters everywhere except in a bc1 address, so paste rather than retype.

total_value_btc.description: What every one of the address's coins adds up to - the whole set, not just this page. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_value_sats.description: What every one of the address's coins adds up to - the whole set, not just this page. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

unspent_outputs.description: The coins in this page, pending first then newest.

items.description: One unspent output: a single coin sitting at the address, whole and ready to be spent. A balance is the sum of these.

list_block_transactions.display_str_template: List the transactions in Bitcoin block {0}.

count.description: How many records are in this page.

has_more.description: Whether there are more records after this page.

next_offset.description: The 'skip' value that fetches the next page, or null when this is the last one.

total_count.description: How many there are in total, across every page.

transactions.description: The transactions in this page, in the order they were mined.

items.description: One Bitcoin transaction. The same shape wherever it was found - looked up on its own, on an address, or read out of a block.

block_hash.description: The hash of the block it was mined into, or null while pending.

block_height.description: The number of the block it was mined into, or null while pending.

block_time.description: When that block was mined. As unix seconds.

block_time_iso.description: When that block was mined. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

confirmations.description: How many blocks have been mined on top of it, counting its own. 0 while it is still waiting. Six is the usual bar for treating a payment as final; one is enough for most everyday amounts.

confirmed.description: Whether this is in a block yet. False means it is still waiting in the mempool: broadcast and seen by the network, but not settled.

explorer_url.description: Its page on mempool.space, for a person to open.

fee_btc.description: What the sender paid the miner to include it. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

fee_rate_sat_vb.description: What it paid per virtual byte, in sat/vB - the unit every fee estimate is quoted in, so this compares directly against 'Get recommended fees'.

fee_sats.description: What the sender paid the miner to include it. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

input_count.description: How many inputs it has, in total.

inputs.description: Its inputs, up to the first 25. Almost every transaction has a handful.

items.description: One input: a coin this transaction spent, and where it came from.

address.description: The address the money came from. Null for newly minted coin and for the handful of outputs that have no address form.

from_output_index.description: Which output of that transaction this coin was.

from_txid.description: The transaction this coin came out of.

is_new_coin.description: True for the miner's reward, which is newly created bitcoin rather than a spend of anything, and so has no source address.

replaceable.description: Whether this input was marked as replaceable, letting the sender replace the transaction with a higher-fee one.

value_btc.description: What this input was worth. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

value_sats.description: What this input was worth. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

inputs_truncated.description: True when it has more inputs than are listed above. The input count is always the real one.

output_count.description: How many outputs it has, in total.

outputs.description: Its outputs, up to the first 25.

items.description: One output: money this transaction paid out, and to where.

address.description: The address paid. Null when the output is data rather than a payment - see the type below.

output_index.description: Its position in the transaction, counting from 0. This is what 'Check whether outputs have been spent' reports against.

type.description: How the output is locked, in the service's own shorthand: v0_p2wpkh, v1_p2tr, p2pkh, op_return and so on.

type_label.description: The same thing in words: 'Native SegWit (P2WPKH)', 'Taproot (P2TR)', 'Data, not a payment (OP_RETURN)'.

value_btc.description: What was paid to it. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

value_sats.description: What was paid to it. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

outputs_truncated.description: True when it has more outputs than are listed above.

replaceable.description: True while the sender can still replace this transaction with a higher-fee one, which is why a payment is not final until it confirms. Meaningless once confirmed.

size_bytes.description: Its size on disk, in bytes.

total_out_btc.description: The total it paid out, across all outputs. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_out_sats.description: The total it paid out, across all outputs. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

txid.description: Its 64-character transaction id, which is how it is referred to everywhere. 'Get a transaction' takes one of these.

vsize.description: Its virtual size in vB, which the fee rate is quoted against.

weight.description: Its weight units, the measure blocks are filled by.

list_mining_pools.description: List the mining pools that found Bitcoin's blocks over a period you choose, ranked by how many they mined and what share of the network that is. Mining concentration is the number people watch about Bitcoin's health, and it shifts week to week - so this is the step behind a mining report or a concentration alert. No API key required.
list_mining_pools.name: list_mining_pools

parameters.description: How far back to count blocks. A short window shows who is mining right now and swings about; a long one shows the settled picture. Last week unless you say otherwise.
parameters.name: period

count.description: How many pools mined at least one block in the window.

hashrate_eh_s.description: The network's estimated hashrate at the end of the window, in exahashes per second.

period.description: The window these figures cover, e.g. 1w.

period_label.description: The same window in words, e.g. 'Last week'.

items.description: One mining pool, and how much of the network it mined.

blocks_mined.description: How many blocks it found in the period.

empty_blocks.description: How many of its blocks carried no transactions but the reward. A handful is normal; a lot is worth looking at.

name.description: The pool's name, e.g. 'Foundry USA'. 'Unknown' covers every block whose miner could not be identified.

rank.description: Its place in the ranking, 1 being the pool that mined the most.

share_percent.description: What share of all the blocks mined in the period that is, as a percentage. This is the figure mining concentration is discussed in.

total_blocks.description: How many blocks were mined in that window, across every pool. The shares below are of this.

list_recent_blocks.description: List the blocks most recently mined, newest first, each with its miner, its fees and how many transactions it settled. A block arrives about every ten minutes, so this is what a 'what's happened on Bitcoin lately' digest reads, and how a workflow notices a new block. No API key required.
list_recent_blocks.name: list_recent_blocks

parameters.description: Optional. How many blocks to return, between 1 and 15. 15 by default.
parameters.name: limit

blocks.description: The most recently mined blocks, newest first. Mempool.space publishes the last 15; older ones are reached by height with 'Get a block'.

items.description: One block: a batch of transactions settled onto the chain.

difficulty.description: How hard it was to mine, at the difficulty in force then.

height.description: Its number, counting from the first block ever mined. This is what people mean by 'block 800,000'.

median_fee_rate_sat_vb.description: The middle fee rate paid by the transactions in it, in sat/vB.

merkle_root.description: The fingerprint of everything in it.

mined_by.description: The mining pool that found it, e.g. 'Foundry USA'. 'Unknown' where the pool cannot be identified, and null for the few blocks mempool.space has not attributed.

previous_block_hash.description: The hash of the block before it, which 'Get a block' also takes.

reward_btc.description: What the miner earned: the block subsidy plus those fees. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

reward_sats.description: What the miner earned: the block subsidy plus those fees. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

timestamp.description: When it was mined. As unix seconds.

timestamp_iso.description: When it was mined. As an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-31T12:00:00+00:00. This is the one to show a person, and the one to feed into a date-and-time field.

total_fees_btc.description: What every transaction in it paid in fees. In bitcoin. The same amount as the satoshi figure beside it, converted for reading.

total_fees_sats.description: What every transaction in it paid in fees. In satoshis - the whole-number unit Bitcoin counts in, a hundred million to the bitcoin. This is the exact figure; use it for any arithmetic.

validate_address.description: Check whether a Bitcoin address is real before anything is sent to it, and find out what kind it is. Bitcoin payments cannot be reversed and a mistyped address is money gone, so this is the step to put in front of one. An invalid address is an answer here, not a failure, so a workflow can branch on it and stop. No API key required.
validate_address.display_str_template: Check that Bitcoin address {0} is valid.
validate_address.name: validate_address

parameters.description: The address to look at, exactly as it was given to you. Bitcoin has several address formats and all of them work here: bc1q… and bc1p… (the modern ones), and the older 1… and 3…. Capitalisation matters everywhere except in a bc1 address, so paste rather than retype.
parameters.name: address

address.description: The address, as the network reads it.

explorer_url.description: Its page on mempool.space, when it is valid.

reason.description: Why it was rejected - a bad checksum, the wrong length. Null when it is valid.

type.description: What kind it is: 'Taproot (P2TR)', 'Native SegWit (P2WPKH)', 'Script hash (P2SH)', 'Legacy (P2PKH)'. Null when it is not valid.

valid.description: Whether this is a real Bitcoin address. This is the field to branch on.

description: Read the Bitcoin blockchain with Mempool.space, the open-source Bitcoin explorer and mempool visualiser. Check what an address holds, watch it for incoming money, follow a transaction until it confirms, and see the individual coins behind a balance. Get the bitcoin price now or at any past moment, what a transaction needs to pay to confirm, how congested the network is, and where mining difficulty is heading. Look up any block by height or hash, see what it settled, and rank the pools mining Bitcoin over any window. Every amount comes in both satoshis and bitcoin, every time as a readable timestamp, and every record with a link a person can open. Every step only reads, so no workflow can move your bitcoin. No account or API key required.
